inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average 146.054m NYSE shares (FY2026 10-K, 'Diluted weighted average shares', note on EPS) x 10 = 1,460.54m ASX CDIs, because the quote is AUD per CDI (10 CDIs = 1 NYSE share). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count. Year-end basic count is lower after USD 700m of FY2026 buybacks, so the diluted weighted average is the conservative choice. Per-CDI values x 10 give per-NYSE-share values.
inputs.debt_basis: USD 260.0m short-term + USD 400.0m long-term (FY2026 10-K note 8, gross), net of issuance costs = 659.365; lease liabilities of USD 166.6m EXCLUDED (see lease_treatment). Cash = cash and cash equivalents only, 30 June 2026, already net of the June 2026 Noctrix acquisition (FY2026 business acquisitions USD 350.7m).
inputs.interest_income_basis: NET interest income (income USD ~77m less interest paid USD 27.1m = USD 49.914m, FY2026 10-K income statement 'Interest income (expense), net'). Stripped because net cash of USD 810m is added to EV in the bridge; the net figure matches the net-cash bridge. History is unlevered the same way (net interest added back in the FY2017-FY2024 net-expense years).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement 'Stock-based compensation costs (note 10)' USD 104.348m plus equity-award tax withholding USD 21.833m from financing activities (no combined adjusted-EBITDA figure published, so the two lines are summed). Metrics.csv StockBasedComp + kpis EquityAwardTaxes.
inputs.buyback_note: Financing-activity repurchases: USD 150.0m FY2024, 300.0m FY2025, 700.0m FY2026. The flat count is funded, not a convention: buybacks exceed SBC ~5x.
inputs.fx_note: USD -> AUD at 1/0.7016 = 1.42531 (Yahoo AUDUSD=X, 2026-09-25T04:32Z). Filings and flows are USD; the ASX quote is AUD per CDI. Parity check against the NYSE primary listing: RMD USD 221.89 (2026-09-24T20:00Z close) x 1.42531 / 10 CDIs = AUD 31.63 vs the ASX print of AUD 31.535, a 0.3% tie across sessions 8 hours apart, which confirms rate, direction and the 10:1 CDI basis. Unsuffixed per-share values are AUD per CDI; the USD twin is USD per CDI (x10 for per-NYSE-share). refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate; re-derive it if the AUD moves materially.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: US 10-year ~4.2% risk-free, 5.0% ERP, beta ~0.9 for an insurance-reimbursed medical-device franchise with low cyclicality gives a cost of equity ~8.7%; debt is USD 660m against USD 1.47bn cash so the capital structure is effectively all-equity. WACC 8.5%, identical in all three scenarios: GLP-1, Philips re-entry and reimbursement risk are charged in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases: the USD 45m annual lease cost is already inside operating expenses and therefore inside EBITDA (treatment B by construction), so no lease line is added to the flows and the USD 166.6m of lease liabilities is excluded from net debt. Charged once.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing: profitable operating company, device + consumables annuity + SaaS). Not a bank/REIT/LIC. Adaptations applied: (a2) USD filer quoted in AUD per CDI (fx_rate + CDI share basis), (b) leases already expensed under US GAAP, (f) risk charged once in flows/weights. EBITDA margin path is PRE-SBC (FY2026: GAAP EBITDA 2,088.1 + SBC 104.3 = 2,192.4 = 38.8% of revenue) because the engine subtracts the SBC charge separately. FY2026 owner FCF margin 26.1%; the year-1 base build is ~27.5% on 60bps of guided margin expansion and capex normalising from an elevated 2.8% of revenue. Working capital: manufacturer with receivables + inventory > payables, so growth consumes cash (wc_capture -5% of the revenue increase; FY2026 working-capital drag was ~USD 27m on a USD 507m revenue increase). Tuck-in M&A (USD 133-351m/yr FY2024-26) is NOT charged against the flows: the growth path is the organic 5-7% guidance, and acquisitions are treated as discretionary capital allocation, which is a mild flattering of value stated here rather than hidden. Historical FCF CAGRs are inflated by the FY2021-23 inventory-build/tax-timing trough and should not be read as run-rate growth.

equity_bridge.note: USD 490m all-cash sale agreed June 2026, expected to close Q1 FY2027, i.e. after the 30 June 2026 balance sheet. Included because the FY2027 5-7% growth guidance already nets out the divested revenue, so the flows exclude MatrixCare while the June cash excludes the proceeds. Haircut ~4% for transaction costs; MatrixCare was acquired for USD 750m in 2018, so a taxable gain is unlikely. Remove this line and rebuild if the deal breaks.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 guidance midpoint (5-7% core revenue growth, Q4 FY2026 call). Equity CAGR (16.8-17.9%) rejected: it diverges >30% from revenue (10-12%) because earnings are retained faster than revenue grows, and the FY2023-26 revenue CAGR embeds Philips-recall share gains that are lapping.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR 16.8%/17.9% exceeds revenue CAGR 10.2%/12.1% by >30%: retained earnings plus FY2025-26 margin expansion, not a faster-growing business. EPS 5-yr CAGR (26.3%) is off an FY2021 base depressed by a USD 255m tax-settlement charge.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes - net interest income): FY2021 543.5, FY2022 120.9, FY2023 519.2, FY2024 1258.5, FY2025 1547.8, FY2026 1473.4 (USD m). Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are within 1pp of each other, so SBC is not outgrowing cash flow (SBC 2.0-2.2% of revenue throughout). Both FCF CAGRs are inflated by the FY2021-23 trough (FY2022 OCF hit by a USD 653m working-capital/inventory build and USD 478m of cash tax including a settlement); the FY2024-26 step-up is normalisation plus margin expansion, not a 40% growth business.

base.growth_note: FY2027 = guidance midpoint 6% (includes ~130bps Astral field-correction drag and MatrixCare divestiture dilution); FY2028 rebounds to 7% as those lap (CFO's 'north of 6% to north of 8%' underlying), then decelerates 0.5pp/yr as Philips normalises and GLP-1 trims new-patient starts toward the 2.5% terminal rate.
base.margin_note: Pre-SBC EBITDA 38.8% FY2026 actual; gross-margin expansion (59.4% -> 61.1% FY2025-26, guided to continue) carries it to 41% by FY2031 and holds. D&A converges from 3.5% (includes acquired-intangible amortisation) toward capex at ~2.7-2.9%.
base.tax_note: FY2026 cash taxes paid USD 357.2m / pretax USD 1,919.4m = 18.6%; current tax expense 20.4%; GAAP effective 20.6%. Pillar Two minimum tax flagged by the company as material; ramp from 20.5% to 21.5% as Singapore/Australia incentives are floored at 15%.

bull.growth_note: Top of guidance in FY2027, then 9% as VirtuOx/NightOwl diagnosis funnel and GLP-1-driven OSA screening lift new-patient starts; Philips stays constrained; Noctrix adds an adjacency. Margin to 43% on mask/accessory mix and manufacturing efficiency.

bear.growth_note: Bottom of guidance in FY2027 (Astral correction runs longer), then oral GLP-1s from FY2029 cut moderate-OSA new starts and resupply, Philips re-enters the US at scale FY2028 with price competition, and DMEPOS Round 2028 competitive bidding plus Medicaid cuts compress provider pricing. Revenue flat-lines FY2031-32; margin gives back the FY2025-26 expansion to 34%. Cap 15x for a structurally slower franchise; terminal growth 1.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: ResMed compounds as the dominant sleep-apnea device and mask annuity: FY2027 revenue grows 6% (guidance midpoint, absorbing the Astral ventilator correction and the MatrixCare divestiture), rebounds to 7% in FY2028 as those lap, then fades half a point a year to 3% by FY2036 as Philips Respironics' recovery and GLP-1 attrition of moderate-OSA patients offset the underpenetrated funnel (under 20% of US OSA diagnosed). Gross-margin gains carry pre-SBC EBITDA from 38.8% to 41%; cash tax rises to 21.5% under Pillar Two; capex normalises to 2.5-2.7% of revenue with D&A converging on it; buybacks keep the count flat and are charged as SBC. USD 470m of MatrixCare proceeds enter the bridge because guidance already strips the divested revenue.
scenario_narratives.bull: GLP-1s remain a funnel tailwind, not a headwind: ResMed's own 2.5m-patient data (GLP-1 users >10% more likely to start CPAP, higher resupply) holds through the oral generation, VirtuOx/NightOwl convert more of the 936m undiagnosed, Philips never regains its pre-recall US share and Noctrix opens a restless-legs adjacency. Growth runs 8.5-9% through FY2030, margin reaches 43% on mask mix and manufacturing scale, terminal growth 3%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The two structural axes both turn: oral GLP-1s (cheaper, no injection) reach mass adoption from FY2029 and reduce moderate-OSA incidence and resupply compliance, while Philips completes its consent-decree remediation and re-enters the US in FY2028 with price competition, just as DMEPOS Round 2028 competitive bidding and the ~USD 930bn Medicaid cut squeeze HME provider economics. Revenue stalls FY2031-32, pre-SBC EBITDA margin gives back the FY2025-26 expansion to 34%, the terminal multiple is capped at 15x and terminal growth is 1.5%. The balance sheet (USD 810m net cash) keeps this a valuation problem, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% house default) because GLP-1/anti-obesity drugs are a genuine, unresolved structural threat to the addressable market over the 10-year horizon and Philips' US re-entry timing is unknowable; bull 25% (below the 35% default) because it requires three independent things to hold at once, GLP-1 staying a net tailwind, Philips staying impaired, and margin expanding a further 4pp from an already-record level. Base 50% sits on management's first formal guidance, which historically has been conservative.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the owner cash flow of a razor/razor-blade medical annuity: SBC and equity-award taxes expensed with a flat CDI count, net interest stripped against the net-cash bridge, US GAAP leases left in opex, margins built from components (pre-SBC EBITDA, D&A, cash tax, capex, growth-driven working capital) rather than carried forward. Discount USD flows at a USD 8.5% WACC, cap the terminal multiple at 20x (15x in the bear), convert per-CDI values to AUD at a dated, parity-checked rate. Tuck-in M&A is treated as discretionary and not charged, which is the one place the model leans generous.
key_risks_to_valuation: GLP-1 (especially oral) adoption shrinking OSA prevalence or CPAP compliance over the horizon; the bear case is the only scenario that prices this and it carries 25%
Philips Respironics' full US market re-entry reversing the post-2021 share gain and reintroducing device price competition
US reimbursement: DMEPOS competitive bidding Round 2028, Physician Fee Schedule cuts, Medicaid funding reductions
Terminal value is ~55-60% of base EV; each 1pp of WACC is worth roughly 15% of value
AUD/USD: a 10% AUD appreciation cuts the AUD per-CDI value 10% with no change in the business; the fx_rate is dated and not refreshed by refresh_price.py
MatrixCare sale (USD 470m in the bridge) not closing; Astral field correction running longer or wider than the guided ~130bps/USD 0.15 EPS
Acquisition spend (USD 133-351m/yr) not charged to the flows: if growth depends on it, owner FCF is overstated by ~2-6% of revenue in those years

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for RMD.AX at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 25.50-43.29 AUD. NYSE RMD and AUDUSD=X from the same API for the parity check in inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: RMD.AX_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, USD millions, FY2015-FY2026) and kpis (CashTaxesPaid, EquityAwardTaxes, InterestIncomeNet, ShareRepurchases, DividendsPaid, Depreciation); FY2026 10-K (RMD.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt) for diluted shares, debt notes, lease liabilities, acquisitions and the tax note.
data_sources.qualitative: RMD.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-25): FY2027 guidance from the Q4 FY2026 call (5-7% core revenue growth, non-GAAP EPS USD 12.00-12.25), GLP-1 evidence, Philips consent decree, Astral correction, VirtuOx/Noctrix acquisitions and the MatrixCare divestiture.
